name: How is a curbless shower actually installed from start to finish?

mainEntity.name: How is a curbless shower actually installed from start to finish?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A curbless shower is built by creating a sloped shower floor that meets the bathroom floor without a raised threshold, then tying the waterproofing into the surrounding floor and walls. The exact method depends on whether the bathroom has wood framing, a concrete slab, or an existing pan.

The construction sequence commonly includes demolition, drain and plumbing work, floor preparation, slope formation, waterproofing, testing, tile installation, and glass or door installation. Elite Remodeling & Design’s published remodeling process can include design development, material selections, permitting coordination, construction, and final inspection.

Key factors:
- The drain must be positioned so water flows away from the entry.
- The shower membrane and corners require careful detailing.
- A linear drain can simplify some layouts but is not automatically the right choice.

Ask for a written description of the floor buildup and waterproofing system before work begins. Confirm who handles plumbing coordination, inspections, and changes discovered after demolition.

A coordinated design-build process is useful when the shower affects flooring, walls, fixtures, ventilation, or electrical work.
acceptedAnswer.description: Installation usually involves demolition, drain and plumbing preparation, floor recessing or buildup, a precisely sloped shower base, waterproofing, testing, tile, and glass. The method changes with wood framing, concrete slabs, existing plumbing, and the selected drain.
